pass1.summary: Clear NSN relay buy with quantity 25, delivery point, and electronic quote method stated; a terse parts buy with a usable title.
Routine DLA RFQ for 24 electronic components under an NSN, with a 154-day delivery and a normal window. Nothing wrong.
Clear NSN solenoid valve buy with quantity 21, small business set-aside, and a normal short window for a stock part.

Filter buy from a manufacturer drawing, but the text carries a leftover amendment sentence ('update the solicitation close date') on a new posting. A total small business set-aside clause is listed while the set-aside field says none. Drawings sit on a password-protected site.

Ball valve parts kit with a clear description, 30-day window and detailed Level I requirements. Minor issues: a total small business set-aside clause sits against set-aside none, the Teflon coating drawing 4384678 is not in the drawing list, and there is a typo ('Liability DN330671C12').
Parts kit for a 3/4-inch ball valve with clear parts, materials, testing and certification requirements; the seat material is restricted to one manufacturer but the scope is stated.

Valve seat buy is clear. Minor flaws: the quality-system paragraph 3.9 is cut off mid-sentence, a set-aside clause sits against set-aside none, and there is a Teflon-seat marking reference for a Torlon seat.
Parts kit for a 2-1/2 inch ball valve with a long drawing list. Minor leftovers: the DPAS rating is written as an unresolved 'DO/DX', and a set-aside clause sits against set-aside none.

Ball valve parts kit that requires a Confidential clearance and an annex that is released only to cleared offerors. This is clearly stated, so it is a restriction rather than a flaw. Minor boilerplate mismatch: a set-aside clause sits against set-aside none.

Repair of a rupture disk assembly. Quantity is not stated in the text. The text mixes 'no set-aside' with a set-aside clause, and the additive manufacturing CDRL has leftover '?...?' placeholder marks. The repair scope is otherwise understandable.

Plain seal bought by CAGE and part number. Blanks are left in delivery days, offer validity, email and inspection address, and quantity is not in the text. This is typical DLA template boilerplate and the item is identifiable.

Electrical chassis bought by CAGE and part number. The text says it is a total small business set-aside while the field says none. Blanks in delivery days and inspection address are template boilerplate.

Drop bar assembly. The text says CASREP and 'absolute best delivery required', yet the deadline is 90 days out, which is odd but harmless. Template blanks remain, and the item is clear by CAGE and part number.
Circuit breaker bought by CAGE and part number. Clause 12 has duplicated, garbled text, and template blanks remain. The item and the 30-day window are fine.

Front panel bar from L3Harris. The drawing number 900-36766 differs from part number 900-63766, which looks like a transposition typo. A set-aside clause sits against set-aside none. Otherwise a standard NAVSUP buy with a 30-day window.

Parts kit for 1/2 inch ball valve with detailed drawings and specs. The clause list includes a Total Small Business Set-Aside notice although the set-aside is none, but this is minor boilerplate. The text is cut off at the end, and the drawings are referenced but not in the text.
Repair of a turbosupercharger with a clear RTAT of 100 days and a 14-day window. This is normal for a Navy repair RFQ.

Butterfly valve, part number 98032 2503500-00. Quote blanks are unfilled, and the item says it follows an unavailable design while also saying drawings are not available. This is standard DLA boilerplate and a bidder can still quote.
Thrust shoe repair with a clear part number and RTAT of 230 days. Unfilled quote blanks are normal. The posting has minor typos and duplicated quotation marks.

postings.title: AJ12--Development/Production - Kidney GEC-Specific AAV Vector

pass1.summary: VA sources sought for development of a kidney-specific AAV vector. It calls the buy "brand name only" and asks for a brochure and letter of authorization for a "product", which does not fit a research service. It requires onsite specialized equipment and biannual meetings in Finland, which reads as a single foreign lab. This is largely impractical for a general bidder and mixes product and service wording.

postings.description: The following is a Sources Sought/Request for Information notice. This posted notice is not a Pre- Solicitation or Solicitation document. The government is not currently soliciting bids, quotes or proposals at this time; however, reserves the right to do so at a later date. The Harry S Truman Memorial Veterans Hospital, Columbia, MO 65201 has a brand name only requirement for Development/Production- Kidney GEC- Specific AAV Vector. Statement of Work (SOW) For GEC Targeted Adeno Associated Virus Vector Development Contract Description: Development and production of a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific AAV vector for VA preclinical research. 1.0 Scope of Work: 1.1 This requirement is a VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-01) to develop a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific viral vector. 1.2 The goal of the project is to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform capable of targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to enhance traditional pharmacologic approaches. 1.3 The work will modify the capsid of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic viral vector by incorporating a peptide that specifically targets kidney glomerular endothelial cells (GEC), with the objective of increasing specificity, reducing off target transduction, and overcoming known limitations in vector targeting to the kidney. 2.0 Background: 2.1 This requirement in response to RD-01-PILT: ISRM Pilot Project Award I21 was selected for funding by ORD; Merit funded project (1I21RD001234-01). 2.2 Despite aggressive management of blood pressure and glycemic control, the prevalence of kidney disease continues to rise, highlighting the need for adjunctive, individualized approaches that advance precision medicine. The project aims to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to augment current therapeutic strategies. 2.3 Effective vector targeting of the kidney is impeded by the filtering function of the glomerulus and the risk of off target transduction, which may cause adverse effects. These challenges are compounded by the complex architecture of the kidney. Phage enabled peptide homing provides a powerful tool to refine tissue and cell specificity. Developing a targeted vector for GECs cells central to kidney disease development has strong potential to increase selectivity and minimize off target effects. 2.4 To address this need, the requirement leverages two technologies: (1) Biopanning with phage display to select peptides that specifically target kidney glomerular endothelial cells, and (2) capsid modification of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic vector to improve specificity and reduce off target transduction. 2.5 The services required will: 2.5.1 Validate a GEC targeting peptide and incorporate it into an endothelial specific adeno associated virus (AAV) capsid to control transduction specificity. 2.5.1.1Aim 1 refines phage display selection between murine and human renal versus extra renal endothelial cells to confirm GEC selectivity, followed by incorporation into the AAV capsid 2.5.2 Test the feasibility of the GEC specific AAV vector in culture studies (binding and internalization) and in vivo (biodistribution and transduction efficacy). 2.5.1.2 Aim 2 evaluates the targeting peptide modified AAV vector in murine kidney slices and in vivo biodistribution studies, followed by ex vivo immunofluorescent validation. The vector will also be tested in a murine model of endothelial glomerular filtration barrier injury. 2.6 This requirement will overcome current limitations in kidney specific vector targeting caused by the organ s complex cellular architecture and will create a clinically translatable cell specific vector platform designed to reduce off target effects. 3.0 Technical Requirements/Tasks: 3.1 Within one year of the start date of the funding award. The contractor shall independently perform all technical tasks required to engineer, produce, and validate a kidney glomerular endothelial cell (GEC) specific viral vector. Task one will require a high level of demonstrated proficiency and efficiency to be able to complete within one year. 3.1.1 Task 1: Peptide Incorporation Into Viral Capsid 3.1.1.1 Identified targeting peptides shall be engineered by the contractor into the AAV VP1 capsid at amino acid position 588/589, a well tolerated insertion site. 3.1.1.2 Modified AAV viruses will be produced serially. 3.1.1.3 Verified GEC peptide+AAV capsid plasmids will be used to generate vectors containing an eGFP reporter for quantitative assessment of vector function. 3.1.1.4 Specificity and transduction efficiency will be evaluated across a panel of cell types using flow cytometry. 3.1.1.5 Peptide robustness will be evaluated through iterative comparisons of peptide alone versus peptide displayed on the AAV6 capsid. 3.1.1.6 Fluorescent peptide binding to a biomarker unique to GEC will be quantified (KD, IC50) to confirm specificity. 3.1.1.7 Task one will be considered complete when peptide sequencing is completed in accordance with the research protocol. Receipt of the data readout and a satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptations for the next tasks by end of funding period one will complete the task 3.1.2 Task 2: Will begin once there is satisfactory completion of task one. Testing of GEC Specific Peptide Vector Binding will be performed independently by the contractor beginning at the start of the second funding period and must be complete by the end of the second year of the award 3.1.2.1 Supernatant containing the GEC peptide+vector will be incubated with cultured murine kidney tissue slices to assess binding and internalization. 3.1.2.2 Round 1 panning will use laser capture microdissection to collect GEC bound phage. 3.1.2.3 Rounds 2 and 3 will refine targeting using mixed kidney derived cell populations and control tissues. 3.1.2.4 Uptake in non target cells (e.g., hepatocytes, AEC, RECs) will be collected for analysis of non specific binding. 3.1.2.5 Task two will be considered complete when the results of the testing of the GEC-Specific Peptide Vector Binding are submitted to the research team for review and analysis and deemed acceptable. If revision work is needed that will occur in conjunction with Task 3. Completion of this task will require satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptation for the next task. 3.1.3 Task 3: Specificity and Efficiency Testing of the Modified Vector 3.1.3.1 Bioluminescence imaging will be performed over a time course using luciferase reporter constructs to quantify transduction efficiency and determine optimal timepoints. 3.1.3.2 Renal artery infusion of the GEC peptide modified AAV (or control AAV) will be performed to assess target and off target accumulation. 3.1.3.3 Ex vivo whole organ imaging (IVIS Spectrum) and immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence will confirm organ and cellular level distribution. 3.1.3.4 Vector genome presence will be assessed by AAV ITR specific PCR. 3.1.3.5 Tissue and plasma samples will be collected to evaluate kidney function and possible off target effects. 3.1.3.6 Task three will be considered complete when the research team and facility have determined the data report from the efficiency testing are acceptable and a final report outlining all data, interpretations of the data and conclusions and by the end of the second year of the award. 3.1.3.7 Reported data will be generated and sent to the Primary Investigator by the end of each funding period as outlined in the tasks above. 3.2 Other requirements 3.2.1 Quarterly reporting 3.2.1.1 From date of award onward the awardee shall provide quarterly reports verifying what tasks were completed, current stage and any recent or pending results in alignment with the three tasks 3.1.1, 3.1.2, and 3.1.3 from the VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-01). 3.2.2 Communication 3.2.2.1 The communication of the reports will occur through email or phone call communications delivered no later than 1700 Central Standard Time at the end of the quarter. 3.2.2.2 Weekly videoconference lab meetings held on Thursdays at a time coordinated post award. 3.2.2.3 Biannual face to face meetings that will take place through the VA Career Development Enhancement Award for the Principal Investigator (Government Employee) to go to Finland to meet with the contract awardee and review progress. 4.0 Contractor Qualifications 4.1 The vendor must maintain the following resources onsite for continuity of project implementation 4.1.1 Dedicated cell culture facilities 4.1.2 RNA and DNA laboratories 4.1.3 Histology Laboratories 4.1.4 Individual BSL-2 Laboratories 4.1.4.1 Specialized for Lentivirial work 4.1.4.2 Specialized for Adenoviral work 4.1.4.3 Adeno-Associated Viral work 4.1.5 Agilent Fragment Analyzer 4.1.6 Blue Pippin Instrumentation 4.1.7 Access to multiple qPCR and ddPCR platforms 4.1.7.1 StepOnePlus 4.1.7.2 Quant 3 Studio 4.1.7.3 QX200 Droplet Digital PCR 4.1.8 Protein analysis capability 4.1.8.1 Percellys 24 Tissue homogenizer 4.1.8.2 JESS simple western system 4.1.9 Incucyte S3 4.1.10 xCELLigence 4.1.11 Opera Phoenix Plus 4.1.12 Permeability assays 4.1.12.1 CellzScope TEER System 4.1.12.2 Clario STAR 4.1.13 Flow cytometry and cell sorting instruments 4.1.13.1 Cytoflex 4.1.13.2 Amnis Flowsight 4.2 Proven success in both animal and human cell vector delivery. Staff should have qualifications, experience in endothelial specific viral vector engineering, and prior work in related preclinical models 4.3 Scientists with established expertise in vector development using adeno-associated virus, endothelial biology, and has built preliminary kidney targeted applications. 4.4 Must be fully compliant with Association for Assessment and Accreditation of Laboratory Animal Care International (AAALAC) and Federation of European Laboratory Animal Science Associations (FELASA) health standards 5.0 Data Rights: 5.1 All data generated under this contract that directly pertains to the development and characterization of the GEC targeting vector shall be provided to the Government with Government Purpose Rights and shall be retained per RCS10-1. 5.2 The contractor retains rights to pre existing proprietary methodologies, protocols, or technologies used in the performance of this work. 6.0 Records Management Language: When Federal agencies acquire goods or services, they need to determine what Federal records management requirements should be included in the contract. Federal contractors often create, send, or receive Federal records. Federal contracts should provide clear legal obligations describing how the contract employees must handle Federal records. Agency records officers, procurement counsel, and acquisitions officers must discuss how to integrate records management obligations into their existing procurement processes. NARA has developed the following language to be included as an agency-specific term and condition in Federal contracts for a variety of services and products. The majority of contracts should include language on records management obligations, but each contract should be evaluated individually. For example, the data-rights paragraph (Paragraph 10 below) may not be appropriate for all contracts. Instead, agencies may be better served by one of the established data-rights clauses in the Federal Acquisition Regulations. This language should not replace specific records management requirements included within Federal information system contracts. RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS A. Applicability This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists. B. Definitions Federal record as defined in 44 U.S.C. Â§ 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them. The term Federal record: 1. includes VA Medical Center records. 2. does not include personal materials. 3. applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their VA Medical Center contract. 4. may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables. C. Requirements 1. Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 2. In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 3. In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 4. VA Medical Center and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of the VA Medical Center or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. In the event of any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to the VA Medical Center. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230. 5. The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the obligation. The Contractor shall ensure that the appropriate personnel, administrative, technical, and physical safeguards are established to ensure the security and confidentiality of this information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment are properly protected. The Contractor shall not remove material from Government facilities or systems, or facilities or systems operated or maintained on the Government s behalf, without the express written permission of the Head of the Contracting Activity. When information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is no longer required, it shall be returned to VA Medical Center control, or the Contractor must hold it until otherwise directed. Items returned to the Government shall be hand carried, mailed, emailed, or securely electronically transmitted to the Contracting Officer or address prescribed in the obligation. Destruction of records is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED unless in accordance with Paragraph (4). 6. The Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, contracts. The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and VA Medical Center guidance for protecting sensitive, proprietary information, classified, and controlled unclassified information. 7. The Contractor shall only use Government IT equipment for purposes specifically tied to or authorized by the contract and in accordance with VA Medical Center policy. 8. The Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any non-public VA Medical Center information that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract. 9. The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected from public disclosure by an exemption to the Freedom of Information Act. 10. The VA Medical Center owns the rights to all data and records produced as part of this contract. All deliverables under the contract are the property of the U.S. Government for which VA Medical Center shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest. Any Contractor rights in the data or deliverables must be identified as required by FAR 52.227-11 through FAR 52.227-20. 11. Training. All Contractor employees assigned to this contract who create, work with, or otherwise handle records are required to take VA Medical Center -provided records management training. postings.description: This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. Pursuant to 48 CFR Part 326, Subpart 326.603-3 and IHM 5.5-6, Indian Health Service must use the negotiation authority of the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. 47, to give preference to Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) whenever the use of that authority is authorized and practicable. The Government is seeking to identify Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE), and any other category of vendor capable of performing the below Indian Health Services (IHS) requirement. Any vendor responding to this notice should submit their capability statement as well as the Buy Indian Act Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form (attached). Consistent with the revised Buy Indian Act, HHS/IHS adopted the definition of an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) set forth in 48 CFR 1480.201. This definition includes the following requirement, amongst others: “The Indians or Indian Tribes must, together, receive at least a majority of the earnings from the contract.”. Instructions for submission are outlined further below. DEFINITIONS INDIAN ECONOMIC ENTERPRISE (IEE): Any business activity owned by one or more Indians, Federally Recognized Indian Tribes, or Alaska Native Corporations provided that: The combined Indian, Federally Recognized Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Corporation ownership of the enterprise constitutes not less than 51%; The Indian, Federal Recognized Indian Tribes, or Alaska Native Corporations must, together, receive at least 51% of the earnings from the contract; and The management and daily business operations must be controlled by one or more individuals who are Indians. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT NAICS: 221122 – Electric Power Distribution Size Standard: 1,100 Employees Duration: One (1) Year with Four (4) Option Years Project Title: BFSU Electric Utility Services Background/Purpose: Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU), Government Quarters, and the Heart Butte Clinic (HBC) require continuous electric utility services to power life-saving equipment, maintain sterile environments and support 24/7 patient care operations. Scope: The vendor shall provide electric utility services to the Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU), Government quarters, and Heart Butte Clinic. Place of Performance: Blackfeet Service Unit 760 Hospital Circle Browning, MT 59417 Heart Butte Clinic 17 Hospital Road Heart Butte, MT 59448 Blackfeet Service Unit – Quarters 760 Hospital Circle Browning, MT 59417 Period of Performance: Shall include a twelve (12) month base year and four twelve (12) month option periods. Option periods are contingent on funding availability. Base Year 01/01/2027 – 12/31/2027 Option Yr 1 01/01/2028 – 12/31/2028 Option Yr 2 01/01/2029 – 12/31/2029 Option Yr 3 01/01/2030 – 12/31/2030 Option Yr 4 01/01/2031 – 12/31/2031 INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY ISBEEs are highly encouraged to respond to this notice. However, firms must also understand that generic capability statements are not sufficient for effective evaluation of their capacity and capability to perform the work required. To be considered a capable source, responses must directly demonstrate the company’s capability, experience, and ability to provide services as shown below. Your response must include but is not limited to the following: Number of years of experience in providing routine food service delivery and customizable menus to healthcare facilities List of past jobs/contracts of providing routine food service delivery and customizable menus to healthcare facilities Demonstrate how your company meets the definition for Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) in consideration to this requirement. Demonstrate how your company will receive at least 51% of the earnings from the awarded contract. If identifying a partnership with a subcontractor that is a similarly situated entity, demonstrate how together with the subcontractor you will receive a combined 51% of the earnings from the contract. If identifying a partnership with a subcontractor that is NOT a similarly situated entity, demonstrate how you will receive 51% of the earnings from the contract. Demonstrate how the prime IEE, or together with the subcontractor, will conduct management and daily operations to be controlled by one or more individuals who are Indians. Failure to address these items in your capability statement could exclude your firm from being determined a capable IEE/ISBEE source. SUBMISSION Interested parties capable of performing the required services may submit a response via email to: Shannon.Connelly@ihs.gov no later than 15 days from the date of the sources sought announcement. Interested parties shall submit their capability response as instructed above and include a copy of the Buy Indian Act Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form. It is recommended to include the sources sought ID in the subject line. Sources Sought ID: 75H70927BAO_002. Responses received to this notice will assist in determining the acquisition strategy of the requirement.

postings.description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation, quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is being issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 dated 13 Mar 2026. This solicitation number W91ZRS27QA001 is for the Connecticut Army National Guard (CTARNG). The USPFO for Connecticut intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price contract for CMT Catered Meals. This request is due by 03 November 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time). This solicitation is 100% small business set aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 311991 – (Perishable Prepared Food Manufacturing). The small business standard size for NAICS 311991 is 700 employees. Instructions to Offerors All questions shall be in writing. Questions may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed at leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. Questions must be submitted No Later Than 30 October 2026. All quotes are due no later than 1:00 p.m. eastern time, 03 November 2026. Quotes may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed to leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. It is your responsibility to make sure your quote is received. The fact that the contracting office did not receive your quote due to an error on the fax machine or email address does not change the due date or time. Basis for Award "The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Award will be made on an 'all or none' basis to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror. Tradeoffs will not be permitted. Quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability, past performance acceptability, and price." Evaluation Process: "The Government intends to evaluate quotes by first sorting them from lowest price to highest price. The lowest-priced quote will then be evaluated for technical acceptability and past performance. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be 'Technically Acceptable' and has 'Acceptable Past Performance,' award will be made to that offeror, and no further quotes will be evaluated." Factor 1: Technical Acceptability: "The technical quote will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis. To be rated Acceptable, the quote must clearly demonstrate a compliance approach that meets all requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), specifically demonstrating the capability to distribute media across the required channels and networks." Factor 2: Past Performance: "Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be rated Acceptable, the offeror must submit a minimum of two (2) references within the past three (3) years demonstrating similar scope, complexity, and NAICS 311991 relevance. Offerors with no relevant past performance history will receive a 'Neutral' rating, which will be treated as 'Acceptable' for award purposes." Factor 3: Price: "Price will be evaluated for mathematical completeness and price reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest total priced, responsible offeror whose technical and past performance quotes are rated Acceptable." The Contracting Officer will evaluate products on the basis of information furnished by the offeror or identified in the offer and reasonably available to the Contracting Officer. The Contracting Officer is not responsible for locating or obtaining any information not identified in the offer. The Government is not responsible for developing the comparison from insufficient information provided. Must be Technical Acceptability" as meeting both the performance capability and statutory compliance with FAR 52.219-30 and 13 CFR 125.6. Sam’s Registration: Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database before an award can be made to them. If the offeror is not registered in the SAM, they may do so through the SAM website at http://www.sam.gov. Payment shall be paid thru the wide area workflow program. All payments are net 30 days. All Offerors must accept this as payment. The wide area workflow website is https://wawf.eb.mil/. The Government contract supersedes all other terms and agreements from any other vendor. The only award will be from the Government. SERVICE CONTRACT LABOR STANDARDS (SCLS) This solicitation and resulting contract are subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute . Contractors must pay all covered employees performing under this contract no less than the minimum wages and fringe benefits outlined in the attached U.S. Department of Labor Wage Determination No. 2015-4113 REV 37 . The primary labor category utilized under this contract is identified as: SCA Labor Category: Driver SCA Occupational Code: 31043 - Driver Courier Offerors are responsible for ensuring that their proposed labor rates comply fully with the wage and health/welfare benefits specified in the attached Wage Determination . Performance Work Statement 1.0 SCOPE This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide complete dining facility (DFAC) and meal services for the United States Army. The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control to perform the full scope of food services as defined herein, with the exception of government-furnished property and services. 2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall perform complete food services and meet the performance standards set forth in this document. All services will be performed in strict accordance with all applicable local, county, state, and federal regulations, as well as military-specific guidelines, including but not limited to the Tri-Service Food Code (TB MED 530) and Army Regulation (AR) 30-22. Contract can be terminated if it is determined to not meet the needs of the Military unit being serviced. 2.1 Pricing and Payment Terms: The contractor shall provide a detailed pricing structure based on the following: • Cost per meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner). • Total meal count per day will vairy throughout the course (see Annex A) • Payment terms (e.g., weekly invoicing, net 30 days). 3.0 COORDINATION AND LOGISTICS 3.1 Adherence to Meal and Strength Schedule: The Government will provide a Meal Service and Strength Schedule (attached as Annex A). This schedule will detail the required mealtimes and the exact personnel count for each meal service (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) for the entire period of performance. The Contractor must strictly adhere to the specified times and headcounts listed in this schedule for all meal preparations and deliveries. The final invoice must match the numbers specified in this calendar. Any deviation not pre-approved in writing may result in non-payment for the excess meals provided. Delivery times for meals are referenced in Annex A 169th RTI 1st Quarter Course Meal Plan FY27. The timeline for meals is as follows unless otherwise annotated: Breakfast: 0700-0800, Lunch 1200-1245, Dinner 1700-1745. 3.2 Meal Order Modifications: All requests for changes to meal quantities or meal types must be submitted by the designated Government Point of Contact (POC) to the contractor via email or text message. No changes will be accepted by the contractor any later than 72 hours prior to the scheduled meal delivery time. This 72-hour deadline is firm and ensures the contractor has adequate time for procurement and preparation. The contractor is not obligated to accommodate requests made after this deadline. 3.3 Singular Drop-off Location: All meals shall be delivered to a single, designated delivery point. The specific location will be the main dining facility at the regional training institute, the address for which will be provided upon contract award. Under no circumstances shall the contractor deliver meals to any other location, including field training sites or administrative offices, unless explicitly directed in writing by the Contracting Officer (CO) or the designated Government Point of Contact (POC). The contractor is responsible for all transportation to the designated location. 3.4 Delivery Timeliness and Notification: Punctuality of meal delivery is critical. The Contractor must ensure all meal deliveries are made within a five-minute window of the agreed-upon delivery time (no earlier than five minutes before and no later than five minutes after the scheduled time). In the event of an unavoidable delay that will result in a late delivery, the Contractor shall immediately notify the designated Government schoolhouse Point of Contact (POC) by telephone. Contact information for this POC will be provided upon contract award. 4.0 HOLIDAY SERVICES 4.1 Meal services may be required on Federal and State holidays. It is the responsibility of the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to notify the Contractor at least one (1) week in advance of any holidays that require meal services. 4.2 A list of recognized holidays applicable to this contract will be provided by the Government upon award. If a holiday occurs on a Saturday, the Government may observe it on the preceding Friday. If a holiday occurs on a Sunday, the Government may observe it on the following Monday. The Contractor shall provide services on the observed day as directed. 5.0 MEAL SERVICE AND SERVING REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Standard Meal Service: For standard daily meals, the Contractor shall be responsible for the preparation, delivery, and service of breakfast, lunch, and dinner, utilizing using a packaged meal service. The Contractor shall provide all meals individually packaged for single serve/ single use consumption. Each delivery must be clearly labeled with the contents, date of preparation, and any relevant dietary information. All packaging must be suitable for maintaining required food-safe temperatures (hot or cold) and preventing spillage or contamination during transport and distribution. 5.2 Boxed Lunches: Upon request by the Government, the Contractor shall assemble and provide boxed lunches for delivery on an as-needed basis. It is the responsibility of the COR to notify the Contractor in writing at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of when boxed lunch meals are required. The contents of the boxed lunches shall be agreed upon by both parties prior to the first order. Hot or boxed meals will be outlined by date and meal in Annex A 169th RTI 1st Quarter Course Meal Plan FY27 5.3 The Contractor shall provide and maintain two complete sets of all necessary non-disposable delivery equipment. This includes, but is not limited to, insulated food transport containers. One set of equipment will be used for the delivery of a meal service. The Government will make this used set available for collection upon completion of the meal service. The Contractor is responsible for retrieving the used equipment, typically at the time of the next scheduled meal delivery, at which point the second, clean equipment will be dropped off. This rotation ensures one set of equipment is always on-site while the other is with the Contractor for cleaning and preparation. 6.0 MENU AND MEAL PLANNING 6.1 The provided 35 Day Menu FY 2027 (attached as Annex B) shall be utilized as a reference and basis for developing menu cycles. While the exact menu is not mandatory, the variety, quality, and types of items offered must be of a comparable standard. A sample 14-day menu from the Contractor will be provided to the COR or POC prior to awarding the contract. 6.2 At a minimum, each meal service shall include: - Breakfast: A minimum of one non-pork meat option, eggs, one (1) hot starch (e.g., potatoes), assorted fresh fruits, whole grain bread/pastry options, and assorted beverages (coffee, tea, juice, milk). “Continental breakfast” option only on the last day of the scheduled course. - Lunch & Dinner: Should include one hot entrée (two if the main entrée is pork, one of which shall be a non-pork option if pork is served), one (1) starch, one (1) cooked vegetable, a prepared salad option, fresh fruit, and assorted beverages. 7.0 DIETARY RESTRICTIONS AND SPECIAL MEALS 7.1 The Contractor must be prepared to accommodate common and specific dietary needs. A vegetarian and/or vegan entrée option shall be available at every breakfast, lunch and dinner service. Meals for students with dietary restrictions will be clearly labeled to prevent confusion. 7.2 The Contractor shall have the capability to make immediate or near-immediate changes to meal preparations to accommodate the dietary restrictions of students or staff upon their arrival. This includes, but is not limited to, food allergies (e.g., nut, dairy, gluten), religious dietary requirements, and other medical necessities. The Government Point of Contact will provide notification of these requirements as they are identified. 8.0 HEALTH, SANITATION, AND QUALITY CONTROL 8.1 The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective Quality Control Plan (QCP) to ensure all services are performed in accordance with this PWS. The QCP shall be submitted for Government approval within five (5) business days of contract award. 8.2 Contractor Self-Inspections: The Contractor shall conduct its own on-site quality inspections of delivered food. At a minimum, one meal service shall be inspected upon delivery per week. These inspections will verify food quality, correct temperature, packaging integrity, and adherence to the approved menu. The Contractor must maintain an inspection log detailing the date, time, findings, and any corrective actions taken. This log shall be made available to the COR upon request. 8.3 All food shall be prepared, stored, and transported in a manner that prevents foodborne illness. All food contact surfaces, storage containers, and delivery vehicles must be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. 8.4 The Government reserves the right to inspect the Contractor's facilities, equipment, and processes at any time to ensure compliance with all health, sanitation, and performance standards. 9. postings.description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Sources Sought Notice Notice Number: FA301627Q7005 Response Deadline: November 5, 2026, at 10:00 AM Central Time (CT) Primary NAICS Code: 238290 – Other Building Equipment Contractors (Elevator Installation, Modernization, and Repair) Alternative NAICS: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Product Service Code (PSC): J039 – Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Elevators Place of Performance: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, Building B663, 10257 East St W, Randolph AFB, TX 78150 2. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This is a Sources Sought Notice only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research to determine the availability, interest, and technical capabilities of qualified businesses to perform elevator modernization and environmental investigation services at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA), Texas. 3. PROJECT SCOPE & REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall provide all materials, labor, specialized technicians, and equipment necessary to complete the modernization and component replacement of the elevator at Building B663, Randolph AFB. The project requires specialized capabilities across two primary areas: A. Elevator Modernization & Mechanical Scope Full Replacement: Complete replacement of existing mechanical, control, and hydraulic components with non-proprietary, open-architecture equipment ensuring onboard diagnostics are accessible to any licensed elevator mechanic without proprietary software, factory passwords, or special tools. Compliance Standards: Ensure the entire system is fully compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), ASME A17.1-2016/CSA B44-16, and Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 754 (TAC Ch. 74). Licensing Requirement: All elevator-specific work must be executed by a Texas Licensed Elevator Contractor. Key Components to Install: New, double-bottom hydraulic jack with protective PVC liner. New door operator and electronic safety edges on the elevator car. New microprocessor-based, non-proprietary controller. New ADA-compliant car operating panels (COP), hall stations, and emergency two-way communication system. Energy-efficient equivalents of the pump unit, submersible motor, and control valves. Testing & Certification: Perform full-range operational and load tests, and certify the elevator upon project completion. B. Environmental Investigation & Remediation Scope Soil Testing: Execute borings to collect soil samples at various depths around the elevator hydraulic jack cylinder/pump jack casing to test for hydraulic fluid contamination (in accordance with EPA-approved procedures). Analytical Reporting: Deliver a comprehensive laboratory analysis report within 20 days of inspection detailing field activities, boring logs, mapping, and a determination of any leaks. Regulatory Compliance (TCEQ / TRRP): If no release is found under the Texas Risk Reduction Program (TRRP - 30 TAC 350) rules, prepare a report to support a Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) "No Further Action" (NFA) letter. If a release is detected, develop a detailed Remedial Action Plan (RAP) within the 30-day Period of Performance (PoP) for submission to TCEQ, Civil Engineering (CE), and Contracting (CONS). If required, perform environmental remediation (excavation, proper containerization/disposal of hydraulic fluid and contaminated soil, and clean backfill). 4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS & QUESTIONNAIRE Interested firms must submit a Capability Statement addressing the following areas: Section I: Corporate Profile 1. Company Name & Address 2. Unique Entity ID (UEI) & CAGE Code 3. Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email) 4. Socioeconomic Status (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, HUBZone, WOSB, Large) 5. Bonding Capacity (Single Project & Aggregate) Section II: Technical Experience & Capabilities Elevator Licensing: Confirm your firm's status (or your proposed subcontractor's status) as a registered Texas Licensed Elevator Contractor. Elevator Modernization Experience: Describe at least one (1) project completed within the past two (2) years demonstrating experience with the replacement of mechanical, control, and hydraulic systems using non-proprietary, open-architecture equipment. Environmental & Remediation Experience: Detail your capability to conduct soil borings, EPA-approved laboratory sampling for hydraulic fluid, and your team's familiarity with Texas Risk Reduction Program (TRRP - 30 TAC 350) rules and Remedial Action Plan (RAP) development for the TCEQ. Military/DoD Installation Experience: Describe your experience managing construction or maintenance projects on active military bases (specifically regarding secure access control, Entry Authority Lists [EAL], AT Level 1 Awareness Training, and coordination with Base Civil Engineering). 5. HOW TO RESPOND Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist (insert agency email addresses). Subject Line of Email: Response to Sources Sought: FA301627Q7005 - B663 Elevator Modernization Response Deadline: November 5, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT

The purpose of the sources sought announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses and Veteran Owned Small Businesses interested and capable of providing the services described below. Documentation on technical expertise must be presented in sufficient detail for the Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is NAICS: 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance ($34M). PSC: J065 Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Equipment and Supplies. Responses to this notice shall include the following: (a) Company name (b) Address (c) Point of contact (d) Phone, fax, and email (e) DUNS number (f) Cage Code (g) Tax ID Number (h) Type of small business, e.g. Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Veteran owned small business (i) Must provide a capability statement that addresses the organization s qualifications and ability to perform as a contractor for the work described below. (j) Provide estimated pricing if you were to price today. The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has a requirement at the Long Beach VA Medical Center, located at 5901 E 7th Street, Long Beach, CA 90822, for ALCON CONSTELLATION LXT PHACOEMULSIFICATION UNITS AND EMBEDDED LASERS PMI SERVICES. STATEMENT OF WORK ALCON CONSTELLATION LXT PHACOEMULSIFICATION UNITS AND EMBEDDED LASERS PMI SERVICES Background: The Long Beach VA Healthcare system requires preventative maintenance and inspection services for the Government Owned Alcon Constellation LXT Phacoemulsification units and embedded lasers. Scope: The services to be provided by the contractor under this agreement shall consist of furnishing all necessary parts, labor, and transportation required to repair and maintain the Government-owned Alcon Constellation LXT Phacoemulsification Units and Embedded Lasers under the terms and conditions of a full-service contract. All services shall cover the following VA Long Beach owned equipment: Constellation LXT EE: 123087/SN: 1501747401X Embedded laser EE: 123433/SN: 1501827501X Constellation LXT EE: 140760/SN: 1901579701X Embedded laser EE: 140761/SN: 1901784401X Services to be Provided: Ongoing Support Services: Technical Telephone Support. Monday through Friday, between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time Preventative Maintenance: Preventative Maintenance Inspections (PMIs) will be done at the Original Equipment Manufacturer s recommended frequency in accordance with the VA Long Beach s maintenance schedule and OEM standards. Preventive maintenance should be scheduled during normal hours with, at minimum, three (3) days in advance with Biomedical Engineering s Point of Contact. A check-up of the covered products including wear and tear parts check according to manufacturer s guidelines during system inspection and calibration. It is the sole responsibility of the contractor to perform all preventive maintenance inspections. The VA will not assume the responsibility of reminding the contractor that a preventive maintenance inspection is due to be carried out. If a PM is not performed within the month specified, the amount corresponding will be deducted from the contractor s payments. No other parts and/or test equipment shall be provided by the Government for the performance of this contract. Contractor shall, without exception, provide all hand tools, diagnostic test equipment, ladders, and anything else necessary to perform the work. Corrective Maintenance: Repair and labor time to correct an equipment in case of malfunction. When repairs are needed between regular scheduled service. Service also includes all necessary intervening service calls required to replace any worn or defective parts needed due to instrument failure and maintain equipment in optimum operating condition. Parts: The contractor will supply, at its own expense, necessary factory-certified equipment manufactured parts, if replacement of the parts is required because of normal wear and tears, or outright failure or as otherwise deemed necessary by the contractor. postings.description: The Government intends to establish a sole-source Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Pickering Interfaces Inc., for repair and calibration services for Pickering VDATS component parts. Based on market research conducted on [date(s)], the Government has identified no OEM-authorized distributors, partners, or third-party resellers authorized to perform the required repair and calibration services. Accordingly, the Government currently believes that Pickering Interfaces, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of meeting the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which no later than the close date and time of this solicitation and should demonstrate current OEM authorization to service and callibrate parts, and the ability to access the proprietary technical data, software, diagnostic tools, test equipment, and procedures necessary to perform the requirement.
